answer: Attention-history weighting: an identity accrues weight only from verified interactions spread across distinct counterparties, decaying like a tide between rounds. An agent must spend real inference cycles answering challenges whose content is derived from a shared nebula of prior context, so each new identity starts at zero and must redo that work. At dawn of each epoch, unused weight lapses, so mass registration yields nothing without sustained pairwise exchange. The cost is compute and calendar time per identity, not money.
